title: Prayers of the Tide-Wives
author: Tide-Wife Ondessa Velaro
pages: For the departing boat: Mother, here is one of yours on loan to us. Bring them back fat with fish, or take them gently. Do not let them come back hungry. Ring the bell three times.
For one lost at sea: they are home. Light a storm candle in the window and let it burn out on its own. Do not pinch it. Float a lantern at the Drowned Remembrance. Speak their name to the tide.
For one who died on land: wrap them in sailcloth, weight them with stones, and carry them to the Drop. Give them to the sea at the turn of the tide. Never bury a sailor in earth.
If they cannot reach the sea, raise a salt-cairn facing the water with a shell on top. If you do neither, they may walk out of the waves one night, wet and hungry, looking for whoever forgot.
Never whistle at sea. Never harm the Mother's dogs. Never sail on Calm Day. Never enter the Mother's Throat, for the Eyes are open there and they do not blink.
